evidence.description: The shared instance is declared as a static property on an actor, which can lead to issues with actor isolation and shared state access.

candidates.explanation: While actors provide isolation, using a shared singleton instance (shared) can lead to contention or unexpected behavior in concurrent environments if not managed carefully, as it creates a single point of access for all parts of the application.
candidates.title: Singleton Pattern on Actor

evidence.description: DateFormatter is instantiated inside a computed property.

candidates.explanation: DateFormatter is an expensive object to initialize. Creating a new instance every time the 'localizedMonthAndYear' property is accessed is a performance anti-pattern.
candidates.title: Expensive Object Initialization in Computed Property

evidence.description: DateFormatter is instantiated inside a function that may be called frequently.

candidates.explanation: Similar to the computed property issue, creating a DateFormatter inside a function that performs data processing is inefficient. It should ideally be reused or cached.
candidates.title: Expensive Object Initialization in Function

evidence.description: JSONSerialization is used to parse data into a dictionary, which is then manually filtered and re-encoded.

candidates.explanation: The code performs redundant conversions by using JSONSerialization to get a dictionary, manually finding a key, and then using JSONSerialization again to turn that dictionary back into Data for JSONDecoder. This is inefficient and bypasses the benefits of Decodable.
candidates.title: Redundant JSON Serialization and Decoding
